im-c62-01.h: 아무나 (사람) vs 아무거나 (사물) vs 아무 데나 (장소)

a.h: 아무나 / 아무거나 / 아무 데나 (긍정문: 무차별적 수용)
a.d: Used in affirmative sentences to express that any person, any object, or any place is welcome without preference.
ex: 배가 고프니 점심은 **아무거나** 다 잘 먹어요. / Since I am hungry, I can eat anything well for lunch.

b.h: 아무도 / 아무것도 / 아무 데도 (부정문: 전면 부정)
b.d: When paired with negative predicates (-지 않다, 없다, 모르다), the particles switch to -도, meaning nobody, nothing, and nowhere.
ex: 휴일이라 거리에 **아무도** 지나가지 않아요. / Because it is a holiday, nobody passes by on the street.

im-c62-01.tip: In positive sentences with unconditional choices, use 아무나 (anyone), 아무거나 (anything), and 아무 데나 (anyplace). In negative statements, use 아무도, 아무것도, and 아무 데도.

answers: 날씨가 좋으니 주말에 아무 데나 바람 쐬러 가요.
날씨가 좋으니 주말에 아무 데나 바람 쐬러 가요
날씨가 좋으니 주말에 아무 곳이나 바람 쐬러 가요.

im-c62-01.hint: Use 아무 데나 for any place without preference in affirmative sentences: 아무 데나.
im-c62-01.why: In positive proposals inviting anywhere without restriction, 아무 데나 is correct; 아무 데도 requires a negative verb.

items: I can express open-ended, flexible choices using 아무나, 아무거나, and 아무 데나.
I can differentiate positive open choice particles from total negative particles (아무도, 아무것도).

a.d: Selects a second-best option when the ideal first choice is unavailable ("might as well").
ex: 영화표가 매진되었으니 서점에 가서 **책이나** 읽읍시다. / Since movie tickets are sold out, let’s go to the bookstore and read books instead.

b.d: Offers or settles for a modest minimum so that the person is not left completely empty-handed.
ex: 목이 많이 마르실 텐데 시원한 **물이라도** 한잔 드세요. / You must be very thirsty, please have at least a cup of cold water.

im-c62-02.tip: Use (이)나 when picking a substitute activity with casual acceptance, and (이)라도 when offering hospitable minimum comfort or solace.

ko: 주말에 원래 가려던 야외 미술관이 우천으로 인해 임시 휴관을 했다.
아쉬웠지만 친구와 함께 근처 실내 서점에 들러 신간 소설책이나 구경하기로 했다.
서점 직원이 비를 맞은 우리를 보며 따뜻한 녹차라도 한잔 드시라며 친절하게 건네주었다.
en: The outdoor art museum we originally planned to visit on the weekend temporarily closed due to rain.
Although disappointed, I stopped by a nearby indoor bookstore with my friend to browse new novels instead.
Seeing us wet in the rain, the bookstore clerk kindly handed us a cup of warm green tea, telling us to have at least that.

im-c62-02.q: What next-best activity did the friends choose when the museum closed?

Returning home immediately and going to sleep
Waiting outside the closed museum gates all day
im-c62-02.why: Sentence two states: 근처 실내 서점에 들러 신간 소설책이나 구경하기로 했다.

im-c62-02.q: What kind gesture did the bookstore clerk offer wet customers?
options: Offered at least a cup of warm green tea
Sold expensive raincoats at double price
Demanded they pay an entrance fee

items: I can propose relaxed second-best activities using the casual particle (이)나.
I can offer minimal thoughtful comforts to guests and colleagues using (이)라도.

a.d: Presents two alternative actions, indicating that choosing either option yields no difference.
ex: 버스를 **타든지** 지하철을 **타든지** 편한 대로 선택하세요. / Whether you take the bus or take the subway, choose whichever is comfortable.

b.d: Compensates for an action, replaces an alternative, or balances pros and cons.
ex: 제가 점심을 **사는 대신에** 친구가 커피를 사기로 했어요. / In exchange for me buying lunch, my friend agreed to buy coffee.

im-c62-03.tip: -든지 -든지 is for choosing among options without consequence. -(으)ㄴ/는 대신에 is for reciprocal trades or contrasting trade-offs.

im-c62-03.q: Fix the sentence where an exchange trade-off was mistakenly phrased with the indifference ending.

제가 오늘 설거지를 해 주는 대신에 룸메이트가 청소를 하기로 했습니다
im-c62-03.hint: Use the trade-off substitution connector -는 대신에: 하는 대신에.
im-c62-03.why: A reciprocal deal where one does chores in return for the other cleaning requires -는 대신에.

en: When deciding the weekend club meetup place, members’ opinions split into two.
The president suggested deciding by majority vote whether they go to a quiet study cafe or park outdoor tables.
Ultimately, in exchange for using the cafe this time, they amicably compromised to go on an outdoor picnic next time.

Forced members to pay for private hotel rooms

im-c62-03.q: What compromise was reached using -(으)ㄴ/는 대신에?

im-c62-04.h: 경직된 거절 vs 선택과 절충을 활용한 유연한 대화

a.d: Refuses options outright without offering middle ground, creating friction.
ex: 그건 싫어요. 다른 거 해요. / I dislike that. Do something else.

b.d: Smoothly balances options using (이)나, (이)라도, and 대신에 to satisfy both parties.
ex: 오늘은 시간이 촉박하니 **간단한 거라도** 먹는 대신에 주말에 근사한 곳으로 가요. / Since time is tight today, in exchange for having at least something simple, let’s go somewhere fancy on the weekend.

im-c62-04.tip: Combining polite substitute offers with compensatory promises builds empathetic and polished social communication.

answers: 제가 자료 조사를 하는 대신에 동료가 발표 슬라이드를 만들기로 했어요.
제가 자료 조사를 하는 대신에 동료가 발표 슬라이드를 만들기로 했어요
제가 자료를 조사해 주는 대신에 동료가 발표 자료를 만들기로 했습니다.

im-c62-04.hint: Use the reciprocal division connector -는 대신에: 하는 대신에.
im-c62-04.why: Splitting work responsibilities (task A in exchange for task B) requires -는 대신에, not cumulative -는 데다가.
